name: Shiva Consciousness (modulated 40 Hz 'binding factor')
origin: Pattern credited by the vendor to Dr. M.A. Persinger; Shiva software by Todd Murphy
summary: Murphy's simple Shiva 'Consciousness' session: a modulated 40 Hz signal stepped counter-clockwise around the head at almost, but not exactly, the speed of the brain's front-to-back 40 Hz 'binding factor'. Murphy writes that reports emphasise bliss and joy, and testimonials on the vendor's site mention colours seeming brighter the next day and dream effects.
notes: Coils sit on Murphy's Shiva ring (Fp1, FT7, TP7, O1, O2, TP8, FT8, Fp2; one coil per site instead of Shiva's coil pairs) and step counter-clockwise seen from above. Phase 1 (20 min) is the 20-min version: stop after it, or let phase 2 run for the 30-min version (a 60-min Shiva version also exists). The Shiva signal file is proprietary; it is approximated by the built-in phase-modulated sine, a 40 Hz carrier drifting between about 38.5 and 41.5 Hz every 2 s, so it stays close to 40 Hz without locking to it ('almost in sync with the brain's own binding factor, but not quite'). Murphy says the rotation speed is set 'at almost the same frequency the binding factor sweeps through the brain' but publishes no step times. His technical page quotes Persinger that speeds around 6 Hz 'would involve increments of 20 to 25 milliseconds' and says Shiva's timings avoid the binding factor's exact (25-ms) speed, so each coil is held alternately 23 and 27 ms here (average 25 ms, 200 ms per rotation); this is an inference, not a Murphy specification, and a whole rotation near 25 ms (about 3 ms per coil) would be another reading. The vendor calibrates its Shakti version of the modulated 40 Hz signal at 10 mG (1 µT), the default here. All reported effects are testimonials, and independent double-blind tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005; Gendle & McGrath 2012). Begin with the shorter version; not for people with epilepsy; stop if distressed.
setting: Dark, quiet room, eyes closed, relaxed without meditating or falling asleep. Murphy suggests the 60-min version in sensory deprivation (darkness and silence) for effects during the session.
schedule: At most once a week, never on consecutive days; up to 6 sessions, then a 21-day break. 60-min sessions weekly or every two weeks at most.
